description: Whether the device a disk was mounted from left, for a disk the mount check found online, then not-mounted: with udev, systemd itself unmounts an idle /etc/fstab mount whose device goes, as after a USB reset, and the disk reads not-mounted, which a USB reset alone does not give. 'before' is the device the mount table named at the last check that found the disk online, 'now' what that same name leads to when the disk is found not-mounted. Each is 'there' (the name leads somewhere, through its symbolic links), 'block' (to a block device), 'major' and 'minor' (its numbers) and 'seq' (the kernel's sequence number of its disk, /sys/dev/block/<major>:<minor>/diskseq or its disk's for a partition, which a disk plugged again gets anew; 0 when the kernel gives none). The device left when the name leads nowhere, to no block device, to another device number, or to the same numbers with another sequence number, both known. Nothing known of before, or nothing that tells the same device from one plugged anew, is no departure: an administrator's umount leaves the device where it was, and the disk stays missing.

cases.note: the name leads nowhere: unplugged, or back under another name
the same device: an administrator's umount
the name and numbers taken again by a disk plugged anew, which the kernel numbers anew
another device number, whatever the sequence number says
the name leads to something that is no block device
a kernel without diskseq: nothing tells a disk plugged anew from the same one
the sequence number no longer read: nothing tells
the sequence number not read before: nothing tells
mounted from no block device: nothing known of where it was mounted from
its name led nowhere while it was mounted: nothing known
a device-mapper name gone, as test/loopdev renames one
